title: cairn install lays the journal merge driver in both repos
intention: cairn install configures the cairn-journal merge driver in every repo root on the box (cairn and CairnCommons), re-lays it when it names an interpreter or checkout that is gone, and reports it like every other setup step.
why: Ticket b7d2e05a1c93 made two sessions' artifact journals meet re-linked instead of forking, but the driver lives in .git/config, which git does not carry. It is installed by hand on akiendelllinux only; on any other box git silently falls back to its text merge and the journal chain can fork again.
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth is never silently degraded) and Law 4 (the .gitattributes comment 'the driver is installed per box' is policy until the installer carries it); outline 6.3.5 (any change to what the host is goes through the installer).
how: Add ensure_journal_merge_driver(roots=None, dry_run=False) to cairn/machines/installer/installer.py beside ask_cairn_home and ask_box_identity, and call it from main() after box-identity. It reads each root's merge.cairn-journal.driver with git config, judges it with shlex (names -m cairn.tools.artifact merge-journal, its interpreter exists, its PYTHONPATH is this checkout), and lays a missing or stale one through the artifact tool's CLI.

clauses.claim: a repo whose merge.cairn-journal.driver is unset reads offered under dry_run, and its config is left unwritten
a run lays the driver in every repo root it is given, and a second run reads already_applied
a driver naming an interpreter that does not exist is judged stale and re-laid with this python
a root that is not a git repository is skipped and named in the detail, not red
cairn install --dry-run lists the journal-merge-driver step among its results

decisions.text: D1: ensure_journal_merge_driver(roots: dict[str, Path] | None = None, dry_run: bool = False) -> dict in installer.py, id 'journal-merge-driver'. roots defaults to cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.roots() (imported inside the function). For each root: skip (named in detail) when <dir>/.git does not exist; read 'git -C <dir> config --get merge.cairn-journal.driver'; it is GOOD when shlex.split of it has words[0] == 'PYTHONPATH=' + str(REPO) where REPO is installer.py's parents[3], Path(words[1]).exists(), and the words contain '-m', 'cairn.tools.artifact', 'merge-journal'. Statuses: all good -> already_applied; dry_run with any bad -> offered (nothing written); else lay each bad one with subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'cairn.tools.artifact', 'install-merge-driver', str(dir)], cwd=REPO, env with PYTHONPATH=REPO), re-judge, and return applied, or failed with detail 'RED: ...' naming the root and the stderr. No question is asked: a local git config is benign, as box-identity makes its keys without asking.
D2: main() puts ensure_journal_merge_driver(dry_run=args.dry_run) into results after ask_box_identity and before install(...).

D3: the proof cairn/machines/installer/proofs/test_install_lays_the_journal_merge_driver.py, house runner (each tooth in try/except Exception, prints PASS/FAIL <tooth>, returns 1 on any failure), PROVES {'7cfbc64b2a67': {'1': ..., '2': ..., '3': ..., '4': ..., '5': ...}}. Teeth 1-4 build scratch repos with git init under cairn.tools.scratch.scratch.scratch_dir and pass them as roots; never touch the live repos' config. Tooth 3 writes a driver naming /nonexistent/python3. Tooth 5 calls installer.main(['--dry-run']) with stdout captured and finds the line '] journal-merge-driver:'. The function is imported inside each tooth.

out: cairn/tools/artifact (its verb is used through the CLI, unchanged)
